---

An error budget caps the expected wrong share among stated directions on each criterion. At fixed weights and withholding cost, compare the best feasible report against the unconstrained optimum.

```{=html}

<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["error-budgets"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Loose budget.** Capping score B at .03 leaves 3 reports; the unconstrained best passes at risk .0933.
- **Tight budget.** At .02, 2 reports qualify; the best states 8 of 15 pairs at risk .0939.
- **Exactly three.** Requiring three grades at .02 leaves 0 reports feasible because full withholding is excluded.
- **Both budgets.** Capping each score at .02 leaves 2 reports passing both count-form checks.
- **Zero weight.** Score B has zero loss weight yet keeps its .10 cap: risk .0906, average share .0267, largest error .240 (in Data).
- **No budget.** Optimizing score A alone lowers risk to .0417 while raising score B's wrong share to .237.

<details>
<summary>Model notes</summary>

The example uses independent normal posteriors for six fictional sites. Each budget limits the posterior expected share over stated directions rather than individual pair probabilities. A report that withholds every pair has expected wrong count and stated count equal to zero, so it satisfies homogeneous count-form budgets whenever the grade cap permits it, while its error share is undefined (`NA: no disclosure`).

</details>
